data.description:
# Intake brief: make local GPU utilisation/prefill metrics visible to the usage report

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the proxy usage report to measure **local prefill time**
(dispatch → first byte) alongside decode time, so "GPU busy %" reflects real slot
occupancy and large local prompts stop being invisible.

## Problem statement

`report.md` currently reports `Local model utilization → Busy time = 7h 02m (29.3%)`
and `Total compute (slot-time) = 7h 47m`, derived by pairing **local `Stream
started` → `Stream finished`**. That window starts at *first byte*, so the entire
prefill/prompt-processing phase is excluded.

For large local prompts, prefill is the dominant cost. In the same 24h window
(2026-10-19 07:23 → 2026-10-20 07:23) the proxy logged `dispatch_first_byte_ms` for
every one of the **463** local requests:

| Prefill (dispatch → first byte) | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Samples | 463 |
| p10 | 3.3 s |
| **median** | **61.8 s** |
| p90 | 269.8 s |
| max | 817 s (13.6 min) |
| **Sum** | **14.3 h** |

Examples: `dispatch_first_byte_ms=98697.8 cache_state=warm cached_ratio=0.942` and
`dispatch_first_byte_ms=133126.9 cache_state=cold cached_ratio=0.000` (212 cold /
251 warm in the window). Adding 14.3 h of prefill to 7 h 47 m of decode puts real
occupancy near **79,500 s ≈ 46% of 48 slot-hours**, versus the 16% the report
implies. This directly misleads capacity work (slot count, ctx size, queue
tuning) — including the concurrent slot-count investigation.

Corroborating gaps in the same report:

- `## Decode speed` and `## Prompt eval speed` are **empty** ("No llama-server eval
  timing samples in window"), so there is no independent decode/prefill evidence.
  `llama-server.log*` in the window contains no `eval time` lines (older rotated
  files do, e.g. `llama-server.log-2026-10-07.gz` has 296) — ingestion or build
  verbosity likely regressed, and that must be established.
- The report's TTFT table is dominated by remote samples; local `ttft_seconds` is
  never logged (only `dispatch_first_byte_ms`).
- The prefill phase is observable in the proxy already: 11,050
  `lease_extended_during_prefill` events with `progress=None`, i.e. prefill polling
  works but exposes no numeric progress.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `proxy-usage-analysis` computes and reports **local prefill time** per local
   stream from `dispatch_first_byte_ms` (falling back to the pairing of dispatch
   and first byte when absent), including p10/p50/p90/max and the **window total**,
   with an explicit statement that the figure is slot-time, not wall-clock.
2. `Local model utilization` reports `busy` as the union of
   **dispatch → finish** intervals (prefill + decode), with the decode-only figure
   retained alongside as a separate row, and a labelled lower/upper bound. Existing
   fast/cheap bucketing and concurrency stats keep working on the new intervals.
3. A `Prefill vs decode` breakdown appears in the report (slot-seconds and % of
   slot-time each), so capacity decisions can see where slot time goes.
4. The empty decode/prompt-eval sections are fixed or explained automatically:
   determine why no llama-server eval-timing samples exist in the current window
   (`llama-server.log` verbosity / build / rotation) and either restore ingestion
   or have the report print a named, self-diagnosing reason (log path, files
   scanned, lines matched) instead of an unattributed blank.
5. Unit tests cover: the prefill parser, the union-interval busy calculation
   (including boundary-crossing and unfinished streams), the fast/cheap split on
   the new intervals, and the empty-eval-timing diagnostic path. Fixtures are
   copied from real `/var/log/llama-proxy` lines (`dispatch_first_byte_ms=`).
6. A regenerated report for the same window shows the corrected busy figure and
   the new prefill/decode split, with the numbers in this brief used as the
   expected-order sanity check (≈14.3 h prefill, ≈7.8 h decode).

## Risks / notes

- `dispatch_first_byte_ms` is logged per local request but is **not** identical to
  `dispatch_to_first_byte_ms` (queue wait is split out as `queue_wait_ms`); define
  which interval maps to slot occupancy and document it.
- Unfinished/aborted local streams (2 in the window) have no `dispatch_first_byte_ms`;
  they must be reported as "unknown prefill" rather than silently dropped.
- Changing "busy" semantics changes historical comparability; keep the old
  decode-only number visible and state the definition change in the report header.
data.title: Make local GPU busy/prefill metrics visible in the proxy usage report

data.description:
# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a request that cannot get a local slot to spend at most
**60 s** in the contention queue before it falls through to a remote provider,
so the dead waiting time on the local path halves without losing the
lease-owner retention benefit.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue` fired **1 481** times with
  `reason=local_lease_active` (plus 252 with no reason), every one after
  `queued_duration=120.00s` — i.e. the full budget was spent and the request
  went remote anyway.
- The config comment for `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds` already records
  the same pattern from the 2026-10-19→20 measurement: 4 947 of 5 805 queued
  waits (85 %) were abandoned, and the prefill-ETA guard exists precisely
  because "the wait is a guaranteed loss".
- Local first byte is p50 8.9 s but p90 96.5 s / p99 443 s (n=606), i.e. the
  queue is not absorbing the tail, it is relocating it.

## Proposed change

Single knob:

```yaml
server:
  contention_queue_max_wait_seconds: 60   # was 120
```

- Keep `contention_queue_max_depth: 8` and
  `contention_queue_lease_grace_seconds: 300` unchanged.
- Keep `contention_queue_policy: queue` unchanged.
- No new knobs; no code change expected beyond config/docs if the value is read
  per request (confirm on implementation; document if a proxy restart is
  required).

**Why 60 and not 30:** a separate investigation concluded 60 s is the optimum
for this queue. This analysis has no evidence that contradicts it — the queued
population is dominated by retained sessions whose prompt cache is warm (the
case the retention rule exists to protect), where a 60 s wait can still succeed
— so 60 is adopted. 30 s is the documented fallback if the measurement after
this change shows the queue is still pure loss (i.e. the abandoned share does
not fall).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `server.contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` is 60 in `proxy/config.yaml`, with
   the comment updated to record the baseline (1 481 full-120 s fallbacks) and
   the reason for the value.
2. A queued local request never waits longer than 60 s before falling back
   (test covering the timeout path).
3. Lease-owner retention behaviour is unchanged: the existing retention tests
   (`contention_queue_retention` / `lease_grace`) pass unmodified.
4. Docs updated (`proxy/docs/routing.md` or wherever the contention queue is
   described) and the restart/reload requirement documented.
5. A ≥24 h deployed measurement shows `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`
   `queued_duration` bounded by 60 s and no increase in fallbacks *per request*;
   record numbers on this item.
6. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- Shortening the wait moves some retained sessions to remote earlier; if the
  remote tier is rate-limited (munitoai-free 3 rpm) this can produce 429s.
  Watch 429s and `Fallback triggered ... rate_limited` in the same window.
- If the ETA guard (LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ) rejects prefill projections above the
  budget, a shorter queue only changes how long the request takes to discover
  it cannot be served — that is the intended behaviour.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (budget consumer).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation (why slots are busy for minutes).
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
data.title: Lower local contention-queue max wait from 120 s to 60 s

data.description:
# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want **any** local dispatch whose projected prefill cannot
finish inside the local wait budget to be refused up-front — even when a slot is
free — so we never start a three-to-ten-minute prefill that the caller will
abandon.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- `local_admission_guard` evaluated **2 380** times: 1 965 `decision=admit
  reason=within_budget`, 415 `decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget`. The
  rejected ETAs had median **176 s** and max **876 s** against
  `budget_s=120.0`.
- The guard, per its own config comment, runs **before entering the contention
  queue** only ("Before entering the contention queue the proxy costs the
  projected local prefill … and compares it with the caller's wait budget").
  A request that finds a free slot is dispatched with no ETA ceiling.
- Result: **48 of 606** local dispatches had a first byte after >120 s, and 91
  after >60 s (p50 8.9 s, p90 96.5 s, p99 443 s, max 592 s).
- llama-server prompt-eval durations confirm the cost: p50 16 s, p90 189 s, max
  591 s, at 77–302 t/s depending on size and contention.

So the guard already exists and is calibrated; it is simply bypassed on the
direct-dispatch path.

## Proposed change

1. Reuse the existing prefill-ETA estimator (observed `dispatch_first_byte_ms`,
   keyed by model + context bucket, rolling window — as used by
   LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ) on the **direct dispatch** path, before the local
   request is sent upstream.
2. If projected prefill > the local wait budget, skip local and fall through to
   the next provider in the existing chain with an explicit log reason, e.g.
   `local_admission_guard decision=reject reason=eta_exceeds_budget_direct`.
3. Keep exactly one budget source (`contention_queue_max_wait_seconds`, lowered
   to 60 s by the sibling child); do not add a second knob.
4. Keep the queue-entry guard unchanged — this is the same decision applied one
   step earlier.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A request whose projected prefill exceeds the budget is **never** dispatched
   locally, including when a local slot is free (unit test with a stubbed
   estimator).
2. A request whose projected prefill fits the budget is still dispatched locally
   on a free slot (no regression for the common case).
3. Behaviour is identical to today when the estimator has no samples yet
   (cold start): document the conservative default and cover it with a test.
4. Refusals are observable: log line with the projected ETA, the budget, and the
   chosen fallback provider; counter available on
   `/llama/local/status` if cheap to add.
5. Docs updated (routing/prefill section) and the config comment that claims the
   guard is queue-entry-only is corrected.
6. ≥24 h deployed measurement: local `dispatch_first_byte_ms` > budget ≈ 0
   (baseline 48), p99 ≤ 120 s; record numbers on the item.
7. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- **Estimator quality:** the ETA model is empirical; a mis-estimate either
  refuses work the box could have finished (lost local capacity) or admits a
  slow prefill (tail returns). Log projected vs observed so the estimator can be
  recalibrated, and keep the safety net of the prefill deadline child.
- **Cold start / new session shapes:** a session with a large but unusual prompt
  may project badly; the estimator's per-context-bucket history is the guard.
- **Load shifting:** refusals push work to rate-limited remotes — watch 429s.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA admission guard (queue-entry implementation
  this extends).
- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation.
- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — 24 h measurement methodology.
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
data.title: Prefill-ETA guard on direct (free-slot) local dispatch

data.description:
# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a live upstream stream **never** to lose its dispatch
lease or its slot to orphan cleanup, and when a stream is genuinely dead I want
its llama-server slot actually freed — so the proxy never dispatches new work
onto a GPU that is still busy, and its capacity accounting stays honest.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- **298** `lease_released ... reason=orphan_cleanup stream_abandoned=True`
  events vs only **6** `lease_verified_active ... stream_abandoned=False`
  extensions; i.e. the liveness verification almost never saves a lease.
- Of 118 local streams longer than 60 s, **81** had an `orphan_cleanup` inside
  their span, and the stream then went on to log `Stream finished` between 12 s
  and ~8 min later — the slot was declared dead while it was still working.
- `_query_slot_processing` (proxy/router_helpers.py) queries llama-server
  `/slots` with `STATUS_QUERY_TIMEOUT` default **1.0 s** and returns
  "not alive" (fail-open) on timeout or unverifiable response. Under a heavy
  prefill the llama-server event loop is busy and the query times out: the
  startup and earlier windows show `TimeoutError` from `_fetch_slots_payload`
  in observability.
- Prior work established that `/slots` is exactly the wrong signal during
  long prefills: LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC (`/slots` unobservable during long
  prefills), LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 (progress unobservable under load), and
  LP-0MUGQHPJ50046LV8 (watchdog released the lease but never cancelled the
  upstream prefill). This item closes the remaining hole: the **orphan path**
  still frees the lease/slot without cancelling the upstream stream (`stream_cm`
  is only captured and cancelled on the no-progress-watchdog path).
- Consequence of the bug: `local_active_queries` is decremented and the slot
  registry entry freed for work still running, so the admission guard and
  serialisation gate see a free GPU and admit new long prefills on top of a busy
  one — compounding the tail (1 827 `saturation=prefill` samples).

## Proposed change

1. **Fail-closed on unverifiable liveness during prefill:** mark the record
   "alive" when the `/slots` probe fails or times out and the prefill/generation
   progress signals are inconclusive, instead of destroying the orphan. Use the
   authoritative progress signals (prefill progress / chunk-refresh /
   no-progress watchdog — the same sources the lease-extension loop uses) as the
   primary liveness evidence.
2. If `/slots` is still probed, raise the timeout proportionally to context size
   (a 1 s probe against a busy 262 k slot is meaningless) or drop it for the
   prefill phase.
3. **When an orphan cleanup is genuinely applied** (no-progress watchdog
   confirmed nothing is moving), capture and cancel the upstream stream context
   (`stream_cm.__aexit__`) so the llama-server slot is actually released — the
   no-progress path already does this; extend the same to the orphan path.
4. Keep `local_active_queries` and the slot registry consistent with the cancel.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A stream that later finishes is **never** orphan-cleaned in between
   (regression test replaying a long-prefill trace; counted as 0 of any sample).
2. `/slots` probe timeout or failure → treated as alive (extend), not as dead
   (unit test).
3. A genuinely wedged record (no progress) is still cleaned up, and its upstream
   stream is cancelled so the llama-server slot frees (unit test asserting the
   `stream_cm.__aexit__` path).
4. `local_active_queries` / slot registry stay consistent with actual upstream
   liveness (asserted in tests).
5. Docs updated (dispatch-lease / orphan-cleanup section of `docs/`) with the
   fail-closed rule.
6. ≥24 h measurement: `orphan_cleanup` ≤ 5 % of local dispatches (baseline 298
   ≈ 49 % of 606) and 0 orphan-cleaned streams that later finish (baseline 81);
   `lease_verified_active` no longer near-zero. Record numbers on the item.
7. Full test suite green; commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- A genuinely wedged slot keeps its lease longer if the "alive" default is too
  generous; the no-progress watchdog bound
  (`local_dispatch_max_prefill_seconds`) is the mitigation and must stay intact.
- Changing liveness verdicts alters capacity accounting; the measurement (AC6)
  is the gate before declaring the fix effective.

## Related work

- LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC — `/slots` unobservable during long prefills (root cause
  of the probe failures).
- LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 — progress unobservable under load.
- LP-0MUGQHPJ50046LV8 — no-progress watchdog never cancelled upstream.
- LP-0MSUO6XRP001MCB2 — active-stream verification added to orphan cleanup
  (the flawed fail-open probe this corrects).
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
data.title: Fix orphan cleanup: fail-closed liveness, cancel upstream on true orphan

data.description:
# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want the local model's prefill to run faster, so every local
first byte — and therefore the whole prefill-dominated tail — shrinks without
changing routing, admission or the GPU's other consumers.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- Current launch args for Qwen3 (from `models.ini` → start-llama.sh →
  llama-server): `--ubatch-size 1024`, `--batch-size 8192`, `--ctx-size 262144`,
  `--parallel 2`, `--cache-type-k/v q8_0`, `--flash-attn`.
- Measured prompt-eval throughput: p10 **77 t/s**, p50 211 t/s (20 k+ token
  batches), p90 **302 t/s**; prompt-eval durations p50 16 s, p90 189 s, max
  591 s.
- Sessions reach 170 k+ tokens (`routing_check estimated_tokens=174617`), and
  the proxy always re-sends the full prompt (`force_full_prompt: true` on the
  local-routed models), so llama-server must prefill large tails every turn;
  prefill is effectively the whole local response time (`dispatch_to_first_byte`
  ≈ total).
- Modern ggml prefill scales with ubatch size up to the GPU's compute/memory
  limits; 1024 is conservative for a 120 GB GPU with batch 8192.

## Proposed change

- `models.ini` `[Qwen3]`: `ubatch-size = 1024 → 2048`. (The operator wrote
  "2058"; that is not a meaningful value — this item interprets it as the
  power-of-two **2048**. Confirm on implementation; if 2058 was genuinely
  intended, correct the item.)
- **No TTS isolation**: TTS remains on the shared GPU; explicitly out of scope.
- No routing, admission or slot-pool changes in this item.
- llama-server restart required; the restart empties the prompt cache, so
  sequence the measurement window accordingly (cold bias for ~an hour).
- Verify with the existing benchmark harness before committing to the value
  (logs/proxy-benchmark.log, benchmark-results/, benchmark-qwen3*-*.json) and
  keep a documented revert (1024).

## Acceptance criteria

1. `ubatch-size` is 2048 in `models.ini` `[Qwen3]` with a comment recording the
   baseline (1024) and this item's measurement.
2. Benchmark A/B (same harness and workload as `benchmark-results/`): prompt-eval
   throughput (t/s) improves by **≥ 1.3×** at p90, or the change is reverted and
   the result recorded.
3. Decode throughput does not regress beyond noise (±2 %); VRAM stays within
   budget (no OOM; confirmed via llama-server startup + `rocm-smi`/monitoring).
4. ≥24 h post-change measurement via the proxy-usage-analysis CLI: local
   `dispatch_first_byte_ms` p50/p90 and prompt-eval durations improve vs the
   baseline recorded above; numbers committed to the item.
5. Full test suite green (no code change expected — config only); commit + hash
   recorded.

## Risks

- **Cold-cache contamination:** the restart wipes the llama-server prompt cache
  (40 GiB) — first-byte stats will be inflated for the first hours. Take the
  measurement window after the cache warms, and note the restart in the item;
  do not compare cold first-day numbers with the baseline.
- **VRAM:** a larger ubatch raises peak activation memory. The benchmark gate
  (AC2) plus a memory check covers this.
- **Throughput may be memory-bandwidth bound already on this GPU** (Qwen3.6-35B
  is a hybrid MoE); if so the gain will be small — AC2 is the fail gate.

## Related work

- LP-0MVGHXD59008UOUD — 24 h measurement methodology to reuse.
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
data.title: Raise llama-server ubatch-size to 2048 (benchmark-gated)

data.description:
# Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want a short local turn never to be parked behind a giant
prefill, and a stalled prefill to surface as a fast detour rather than a silent
multi-minute hang — so the local tail is bounded by policy, not by whatever
happens to be first in the queue.

Part of epic **LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD** (minimise local LLM tail latency).

## Evidence (24 h window, 2026-10-20 23:31 → 2026-10-21 23:31 IST)

- `local_max_concurrent_prefills: 1` (LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ) serialises prefills
  for good reason — measured 2026-10-19→20: first-byte p50 **23.4 s** alone vs
  **85.0 s** with one overlap, at **flat** aggregate throughput (~254 t/s). But
  it also means one long prefill is head-of-line blocking for every queued local
  request.
- `contention_queue_wait ... saturation=` shows **1 827** prefill-saturated
  samples vs 468 generating: the pool spends most of its life with one prefill
  blocking the other.
- `lease_extended_during_prefill` fired 6 685 times in the window — prefills
  routinely outlive the lease, and `prefill_wait_exceeds_threshold` fired 450
  times across 119 sessions (first line of each: `waited=30s progress=0`).
- **48 of 606** local dispatches had a first byte after >120 s, five after
  >400 s; the client sees a silent socket for that entire period (no SSE
  heartbeat during prefill), so it cannot distinguish "working" from "hung".
- `prefill_progress_unobservable` logged 1 242 times: the proxy itself often
  cannot say how far a prefill has got.

## Proposed change

Three coordinated behaviours (all previously recommended, none present today):

1. **ETA-aware admission ordering.** Among requests that are admissible
   locally, admit the smallest projected prefill first (shortest-ETA-first)
   instead of FIFO, so a 7-minute prefill cannot park a queue of 20-second
   turns. Lease-owner retention stays the primary tie-break so a returning
   warm-cache session is not starved; ordering applies within each retention
   class.
2. **Prefill heartbeat.** Emit SSE comment/keep-alive frames during prefill
   (e.g. `: prefill 42%` or a bare `: keep-alive` on a ≤30 s cadence, driven by
   the existing progress signal) so clients see liveness and their own
   first-byte timeouts are meaningful.
3. **Prefill deadline with automatic detour.** Add a configurable
   `local_prefill_deadline_seconds` (default ~90). If the first byte has not
   arrived by then, cancel the local dispatch and fall through to the next
   provider, with a log reason and telemetry. This is the hard backstop
   independent of ETA-estimator quality; it must not fire for requests admitted
   legitimately inside their budget, so it is set well above the budget.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Ordering: a queued short-prefill request is not admitted after a long one
   when both are pending and both fit the budget (unit test with synthetic
   ETAs); retention priority still wins over size (unit test).
2. Heartbeat: during a local prefill longer than the cadence, SSE keep-alive
   frames are emitted at the configured cadence, and they stop when the first
   byte arrives (test asserting frame sequence and no leakage into the body).
3. Deadline: a dispatch with no first byte by the deadline is cancelled, the
   upstream request aborted, and the request routed to the next provider
   (test with a stalled upstream stub); no orphaned lease or slot is left behind
   (interacts with the orphan-cleanup child).
4. All three governed by documented config knobs with validation (malformed →
   safe default), no change to `contention_queue_max_wait_seconds` semantics
   (single budget source).
5. ≥24 h measurement: local p99 first byte bounded by the deadline + margin
   (baseline 443 s, max 592 s); longest client-visible silent window ≤ the
   heartbeat cadence; no increase in `contention_queue_fallback_after_queue`
   per request. Record numbers on the item.
6. Docs updated (routing/prefill + streaming sections); full test suite green;
   commit + hash recorded.

## Risks

- **Ordering can starve long prefills** under a stream of short ones. Retention
  wins first, and a long request that keeps losing should still get its budget
  (age-based promotion after N rejections or when its projected ETA still fits).
  Cover with a test.
- **Heartbeat frames** must be valid SSE comments for every client in use
  (pi/opencode/curl) and must not be counted as content by token accounting.
- **Deadline vs adaptive timeout:** the proxy already has an adaptive whole-
  request timeout and a session guardrail; the new deadline must be strictly
  shorter and must not conflict (document precedence).
- This child is the largest in the epic; if schedule pressure hits, ship in this
  order: deadline (safety) → heartbeat (UX) → ordering (scheduling).

## Related work

- LP-0MVGDUUV3001XFRJ — prefill serialisation (the gate this schedules around).
- LP-0MVGDUV5E005UWBQ — prefill-ETA estimator to reuse.
- LP-0MUXQ5QL40027VZ4 / LP-0MUXTW4MD003TVIC — progress-observability limits the
  heartbeat and deadline depend on.
- Epic LP-0MVIPY7QX0027XVD — parent.
data.title: ETA-aware local admission + prefill heartbeat + prefill deadline
